title: Convolution Visualizer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Convolution
Impulse Response
LTI Systems
description: Step-by-step flip-and-slide demonstration of the convolution integral. The impulse response is time-reversed, shifted by t, multiplied by the input, and the area under the product is plotted as the output y(t) for eight pairs of signals.

learningObjectives: Explain each step of the convolution integral: flip, slide, multiply and integrate
Identify the range of t over which two finite-duration signals overlap
Predict the shape of the output for simple pairs of signals
Describe how the shape of an impulse response determines what a system does to its input
prerequisites: Impulse response of an LTI system

equations: y(t) = integral of x(tau) h(t - tau) d tau
assumptions: The integral is evaluated with the midpoint rule and a step of 0.005 s
All signals are zero for t < 0

keyQuestions: Why is the impulse response reversed before it is shifted?
Over what range of t do two finite pulses overlap?
What does the area of the shaded region represent?
commonMisconceptions: Convolution multiplies the two signals point by point
The output has the same duration as the input
The impulse response slides without being reversed
assessmentOpportunities: Sketch the output of two rectangles before stepping through
Compute y(t) at one time from the overlap region
